title: Gauss Law and Electric Flux
notes: **Electric flux $\Phi_E$:** $\Phi_E = \oint \vec{E} \cdot d\vec{A}$. It measures the total number of field lines passing through a closed surface.
**Gauss law:** $\oint \vec{E} \cdot d\vec{A} = Q_{enclosed}/\epsilon_0$. The total flux through a closed surface depends only on the charge inside, not on the shape of the surface.
**Why useful:** for symmetric charge distributions (spherical, cylindrical, planar), Gauss law lets you find $E$ without integration.
**Flux through closed surface:** if no charge is inside, net flux is zero because as many lines enter as leave.
